Claiming this designation in a Vienna manuscript dated 1435-1445 is anachronistic by roughly 150-160 years, the same defect pattern as Cor Caroli/Mira/Alcor from this same source. New finding, not previously flagged by v3_audit.

Per two independent secondary sources: 'Al Najid' ('the conqueror') is documented in Abu Ma'shar's 9th-c. work as a name for CAPELLA (alpha Aurigae), not gamma Orionis (Bellatrix). The transfer of this name to gamma Orionis is specifically credited to 'the Vienna school of astronomy led by Johannes von Gmunden' in the 15th century, with currency in print dated only to a 1492 Latin Alfonsine Tables edition -- Johannes von Gmunden is the same figure this lexicon's Vienna source (HIST_STAR_ATT_0006 etc., dated 1435-1445) is attributed to. Attributing 'al-najid' to gamma Orionis via al-Sufi at 964 AD (over 500 years before the documented Vienna-school transfer) is not supported. New finding, not previously flagged by v3_audit; independently corroborates that this lexicon's Vienna-tradition material is a real, external, documented source of star-name transfer errors, not a compiler artifact confined to this lexicon.

al-Sufi's genuine documented 10th-c. Arabic name for beta Andromedae (Mirach) is 'Janb al-Musalsalah' ('side of the chained lady'; per Ian Ridpath's Star Tales, secondary scholarship following Kunitzsch). 'al-mi'zar' IS a real historical name connected to Mirach, but via a documented LATER path: the modern name 'Mirach'/'Mirac'/'Mirath' derives from a corruption of 'mizar' first attested in the printed 1521 Alfonsine Tables ('super mizar') -- roughly 550 years after al-Sufi (964 AD), and centuries after this row's claimed source/date. This row conflates a real-but-much-later Latin-tradition name with al-Sufi's actual 10th-c. Arabic text. The SAME exact Arabic string is independently and correctly attested for a different star, Mizar (zeta UMa, HIST_STAR_ATT_0194), from the SAME al-Sufi source on a different folio -- implausible for a single careful 10th-c. catalog. This refines, rather than simply confirms, v3_audit F005: the misattribution is about SOURCE AND DATE, not about the Arabic root being fake.
